Use the existing topk_ids/topk_weights as inputs for generation 1, but structure the kernel around per-expert problem sizes so it can consume the scheduling metadata from child 1_0 in later iterations. strategy.evidence_chain: Code evidence: stage2_grouped_down_kernel maps one scalar thread to each (topk slot, hidden column, split), loops over I scale blocks, atomicAdds topk_weights[tk] * partial into out_accum, then finalize_output_kernel casts to bf16. Reference evidence: FlashInfer blockscaled_contiguous_grouped_gemm_finalize_fusion.py is a grouped block-scaled GEMM with fused finalize logic that maps permuted rows back to token/topk indices and loads router_scale in the epilogue; grouped-gemm-deepgemm.md identifies MoE as a multi-problem small-GEMM batching case; FlashInfer grouped_gemm_masked_blackwell.py uses a persistent scheduler for variable per-group M. Inference: the parent pays both scalar GEMV-style compute and split atomic/finalize overhead. Action: make GEMM2 an expert-major grouped GEMM with fused router weighting/final cast.
strategy.expected_impact: Can remove the separate finalize launch, reduce split atomic traffic, and improve locality for gemm2_weights and scales by processing contiguous expert tiles. It also aligns the CUDA candidate with FlashInfer's grouped finalize boundary while keeping GEMM1 unchanged for attribution.
strategy.risks: A full tensor-core path may not be available on the L20D/Ada-like target for native FP4, so the first version may still use software FP4 dequant inside a tiled GEMM. T=1 gives tiny per-expert M, so occupancy and tail effects are serious. Keep correctness by preserving weighted scatter-add semantics when multiple top-k entries map to the same source token.

GEMM1 remains unchanged.
